what: ‹Typesetting› button — pressing it switches the html data-typesetting between serif ↔ sans-serif, swapping the English and body font variables of the whole site at once, and the next visit opens in that setting. The dot in the pill inside the button slides sideways in .2s ease, and the name of the unselected typeface fades to .6 (.3s). Even when there are several buttons, as in the menu and footer, they share the same state.

options.values: Two values, default ‹serif, sans-serif› — the first value is the default face
options.attr: data- name to attach to html, default typesetting
options.key: localStorage name to remember, default kf-<attr>
options.--fx-shift: Distance the dots travel (css variable), default 8px

use: — CSS for the user side: html[data-typesetting=sans-serif] { --site-en: var(--kf-font-grotesk); }
note: The original writes to IndexedDB — the part does the same with localStorage. What actually changes the font is the consuming side’s css html[data-<attr>] It’s a variable

from.where: shared.js Typesetting button in the footer and full-screen menu (BRAND Serif ↔ BRAND Grotesk · Yu Mincho ↔ Yu Gothic — original typesetting module, dot transform .2s ease)
